clue.text: "A cannonball took his legs off, so he _______" (Hood)

definitions.text: "A cannonball took his legs off, so he _______" (Hood)

parts.words: "A cannonball took his legs off, so he _______"
parts.note: surface reading: a soldier maimed in battle who then gave up the fight
setter's reading: Thomas Hood's comic ballad Faithless Nelly Gray, whose line puns on limbs and weapons

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hood's Faithless Nelly Gray opens with Ben Battle losing his legs to a cannonball; the next line puns on arms as weapons and as limbs, since with no legs he puts his limbs on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to put down weapons, and here the phrase also means resting his upper limbs on the floor.

clue.text: "They went and told the sexton and _______" (Hood)

definitions.text: "They went and told the sexton and _______" (Hood)

parts.words: "They went and told the sexton and _______"
parts.note: surface reading: villagers report a death to the church officer, who then does his duty
setter's reading: the last couplet of Hood's Faithless Sally Brown, which puns on told and tolled

explanation.walkthrough: Hood's ballad Faithless Sally Brown ends with Ben's death: the villagers told the sexton, and he tolled the funeral bell, the joke being the near-identical sound of told and tolled. A sexton looks after a church and its bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringing slowly for a funeral is what a parish church caretaker does when a death is announced.

clue.text: Husks of maize — commonplace stuff — I'm embarrassed

parts.note: corn is trite, hackneyed material, as in corny jokes
shucks is a bashful exclamation

explanation.surface: Someone apologising that they have only brought ordinary maize husks, blushing at the modest offering.
explanation.definitionFit: Shucks are the outer leaves wrapping a cob, so those of maize are its outer covering.

clue.text: "The love that loves a scarlet coat should be more ____" (Hood)

definitions.text: "The love that loves a scarlet coat should be more ____" (Hood)

parts.words: "The love that loves a scarlet coat should be more ____"
parts.note: surface reading: a reproach that a girl who loves soldiers ought to be more constant
setter's reading: Nelly's fickleness in Faithless Nelly Gray, with a pun on soldiers' dress

explanation.walkthrough: In Hood's Faithless Nelly Gray, Nelly rejects legless Ben; he says one who loves a redcoat should be steadier, the word meaning both consistent and military dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means unvarying or constant, and a scarlet coat is itself a soldier's regimental dress.

clue.text: Gloss for cold weather?

parts.note: surface reading: shiny paint, the final layer put on woodwork
setter's reading: a heavy garment worn outside in winter

explanation.walkthrough: Gloss paint is applied as the top layer over undercoat, so the decorator's term doubles as the name of a warm outer garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A final layer of paint is a top coat, and the same compound names a thick coat worn over other clothes in winter.

clue.text: Kirby Dynamo can't play anywhere else

indicators.note: to play with something is to toy with it, so these letters are moved about freely

parts.note: the words taken letter for letter, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A small-town football club that has nowhere else to host its matches.
explanation.walkthrough: Kirby is a town near Liverpool, so Kirby Dynamo reads like a local football team; the answer is the protester's slogan, shortened to NIMBY.
explanation.definitionFit: The slogan objects to a development nearby while accepting it in some other place, so it amounts to saying build it elsewhere.

clue.text: Source of oil, thick, keeping Italian boy and girl on a string

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one word holds the others within

parts.note: thick and crass both mean stupid
IT is the abbreviation for Italian
a boy's name
a girl's name
G is one of the strings of a violin

explanation.surface: A dim-witted puppeteer holding a pair of Italian children dangling on a cord.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, girl on a string puts the girl's name above the string letter. The boy, girl and string all sit inside the word for thick.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical plant is distilled for an aromatic oil used as an insect repellent, so it is where that oil comes from.

clue.text: Conservative and Lib-Dem leaders paid on the nail

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
Paddy Ashdown led the Liberal Democrats from 1988 to 1999

explanation.surface: Party chiefs settling a bill promptly, as if politicians ever paid up at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a British political party; their long-serving leader supplies most of the letters, with the Conservative abbreviation in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying on the nail means paying immediately, and money handed over at once is ready payment.

clue.text: Oil changed into wine in French fiddle

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

parts.note: vin is French for wine

indicators.note: something changed has been altered, so the letters come out in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A miracle in which oil is turned into French wine, with a hint of fraud in the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddle is the informal name for the bowed four-string instrument.

clue.text: Nod off when holding medal, more than likely

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so one part goes inside the other
off here means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the Distinguished Service Order, a British military decoration

explanation.surface: Falling asleep at a medal ceremony, which seems quite probable.
explanation.walkthrough: Nod off looks like one phrase meaning to doze; it splits, with off rearranging the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, a favourite priced shorter than evens is expected to win, so the term means probable.

clue.text: Mink, coypu, etc rage round the river? That's right

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the other letters sit inside

parts.note: rage and fury are synonyms
R is the abbreviation for river
i.e. stands for id est, Latin for that is
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Fur-bearing animals in a rage beside a river, someone confirming that is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: That's right looks like an approving aside, but it splits into two abbreviations. A coypu is a South American rodent farmed for its fur.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means furs collectively or the fur trade, and mink and coypu pelts are examples of such goods.

clue.text: Report of marsupial mixing fat and flour

definitions.note: a gerund phrase standing for the mixture itself

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo

explanation.surface: News of a kangaroo stirring ingredients together in a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: This French cooking base is butter or another fat cooked with flour to thicken sauces.

clue.text: Pestering of donkey and humans among deer

indicators.note: being among things means placed in their midst, inside them

parts.note: a hart is a male deer
an ass is a donkey
men as people in general

explanation.surface: A donkey and some people pestering a herd of deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestering is persistent annoyance, and the noun names that kind of repeated hounding of someone.

clue.text: Doesn't let student entrant pay attention after science film

indicators.note: after tells us which part follows which, so the order of pieces is set

parts.note: SC is an abbreviation for science

indicators.note: an entrant is one who comes in, so a letter goes inside a word

parts.note: to hinder is to obstruct, not allow
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
list is an old verb for listen

explanation.surface: A pupil who does not let a newcomer listen once a science film starts.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for science comes first, then the word for prevents with the learner inside it, then the archaic word for listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Steven Spielberg's 1993 Holocaust drama is a famous example of a motion picture.

clue.text: Ensure obedience to the Queen for ceremonial purposes

indicators.note: the phrase is put to the purpose of carrying the letters inside it, run across word breaks

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the third

explanation.surface: Loyal subjects being made to obey the monarch on state occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one royal scene, but the answer is tucked inside three consecutive words.
explanation.definitionFit: To make people comply with a law or rule is to compel obedience to it.

clue.text: See 2
Roman poet cut off in tube

parts.note: Ovid wrote the Metamorphoses

indicators.note: off suggests things knocked out of their usual place, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A classical poet trapped and severed inside a pipe, a gruesome little scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut off reads as one phrase meaning severed or isolated; it splits into the fodder and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This anatomical passage carries eggs from the ovary, so it is a duct, a kind of tube.

clue.text: How many varieties? F-five? Ten? Yes, possibly, but no point

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters could be arranged another way
saying no to something leaves it out

parts.note: the words taken letter for letter
E for east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone guessing a number of varieties, trying odd alphanumeric codes and hedging the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder has one E too many; drop one compass point and rearrange the rest. Heinz famously advertised its foods as 57 varieties.
explanation.definitionFit: The Heinz slogan claims that many kinds of product, so the number answers the question of how many varieties.

clue.text: See 5
Man (say, more or less) and boy in 19 of the end of 1?

definitions.note: in coat of arms, read as dressed in armour

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word, so it is taken for its sound

parts.note: a man is a male
c. is short for circa, about
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A rough-and-ready figure of a man and a boy wearing the heraldic coat at the end of a ballad line.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is COAT and 1 ends in ARMS, so the definition reads in coat of arms, punningly a coat made for arms or war.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad in chain armour means dressed for battle, a coat for warfare rather than a heraldic emblem.

clue.text: See 14
Number attached to Australian rock strata

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
Ayers Rock, the former name of Uluru

explanation.surface: A numbered label fixed to Uluru, with geological bands as the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are horizontal bands of rock or other material laid one on another.

clue.text: Sept, Nov and Dec are fiery

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what these short month names lack to become full words

definitions.note: an adjective standing for glowing remains of a fire
definitions.meaning: second meaning: glowing bits of coal or wood left in a dying fire

explanation.surface: A claim that the autumn and winter months are blazing hot.
explanation.walkthrough: Each abbreviation becomes a full month name by adding the same five-letter ending, so they are short of those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing remnants of a fire are still hot coals, which is a fair stretch for fiery things.

clue.text: Apply poison to make dog stand up

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to arise is to get to one's feet

explanation.surface: Poisoning a dog to make it stand, a nasty bit of animal training.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a South American arrow poison, and the verb means to treat or paralyse with it.
